div.head: IV Eg 1.5a
div.ab: Gif he swa earm bið, þæt he aðer deð oððe þa Godes wanað, his saula to forwyrde, oððe waccor mid modes graman hy behwyrfð þonne þæt he him to agenum teleð, ðonne him micele agenre is, þæt him æfre on écnysse gelæst, gif he hit mid unnan ⁊ mid fulre blisse dón wolde.

Gyf he swa earm bið, þæt he aþer deð oððe þa Godes wanað, his sawla to forwyrde, oððe waccor mid modes graman hy behwyrfð þonne þæt he him to agenum teleð, þonne him micele agenre is, þæt him æfre on écnysse gelæst, gyf he hit mid unnan ⁊ fulre blisse dón wolde.

Gyf he swa earm bið þæt he aþer deð oððe þa Godes wanað, his sawla to forwyrde, oððe waccor mid modes graman hy behwyrfð þonne þæt he him to agenum teleð, þonne him micele agenre is þæt him æfre on écnysse gelæst, gyf he hit mid unnan ⁊ mid fulre blisse dón wolde.

Wenn der [Zehntpflichtige] so erbärmlich ist, dass er eine beider [folgender Handlungen] thut: entweder die Kirchen[-Gerechtsame] mindert, seiner Seele zum Verderben, oder mit Herzens Unwillen sie lässiger behandelt als was er sich zum Eigenthume zählt: bei weitem mehr ist doch sein eigen, was ihm immer in Ewigkeit bleibt, wenn er es mit Bereitwilligkeit und mit voller Freudigkeit thun wollte.

If the [tithe-payer] is so wretched that he does one of two [things]: either diminishes God's [dues], to the ruin of his soul, or with grudging heart treats them more slackly than what he counts as his own property: yet far more his own is what remains his for ever in eternity, if he would do it willingly and with full gladness.

If he is so debased as either to curtail what is due to God, to the ruin of his soul, or, with angry heart, to attend to it less diligently than to what he accounts his own, [he ought to realise that] what endures for him to all eternity will be much more his own, if he has been willing to give his tribute with gladness and with all willingness.

If he is so contemptible, that he either curtails God’s [dues] to the perdition of his soul, or with reluctance at heart attends to them less diligently than to what he accounts his own; then much more his own is what endures for him for ever into eternity if he would pay it with willingness and full gladness.
div.note: Not in the Latin Versio. In F, ‘gerihta’ or similar should be supplied after ‘þa Godes’.

note.seg: ergänze gerihta oder teoðunga oder Synonymes
supply gerihta or teoðunga or a synonym

Dieser Satz fehlt Versio, aber nicht etwa, weil er ihr zu homiletisch schien, denn zahllose damalige geschäftsmäßige Urkundenschreiber lassen durch Schenkung an die Kirche ewiges Leben verdienen; z. B. Bi 1297; vgl. Gl Himmel 4

This sentence is missing in the Versio, but not, say, because it seemed too homiletic to the translator, for countless businesslike charter-scribes of the time let eternal life be earned through gifts to the church; e.g. Bi 1297; cf. Gl Himmel 4
‘arm’ Thorpe, Schmid; sinngemässer ‘wretched’ Kemble. Beispiele für ‘moral sense’ Toller Suppl.: carm I 1a
‘poor’ Thorpe, Schmid; more to the sense, ‘wretched’ Kemble. Examples of the ‘moral sense’ Toller Suppl.: carm I 1a

Hier übersprang Archetyp ein Wort, das materielle Ansprüche auf Geldeinkünfte, vielleicht die Zehntäcker, bedeutete; God (s. d. Wb 15) bed. hier ‘Kirchentemporalien’. Vielleicht fehlt god ‘bona, Güter’ [wofür aus Bibel 2 Beispiele Toller s. v. (auch Bi 330); Godes god wird dort zitiert], und das Auge des Abschreibers wähnte Dittographie. Frühere nehmen keine Lücken an, sondern verstehen þa Godes: ea quae Dei sunt

Here the archetype skipped a word meaning material claims to money revenues, perhaps the tithe-acres; God (see that word in Wb 15) here means ‘church temporalities’. Perhaps god ‘bona, goods’ is missing [for which Toller s. v. gives 2 examples from the Bible (also Bi 330); Godes god is cited there], and the copyist’s eye took it for a dittography. Earlier editors assume no lacuna, but understand þa Godes: ea quae Dei sunt
nicht ‘es vollführt’; hy bezieht sich auf þa; behwyrfð (s. Toller Suppl.) heisst ‘fürsorglich betreibt’
not ‘carries it out’; hy refers to þa; behwyrfð (see Toller Suppl.) means ‘carefully attends to’
Translated ‘erbärmlich’ by Liebermann. See Toller, Suppl. p. 172, s.v. earm, 1 a.

Liebermann suggests that the word god may have been omitted by the scribe, but is this assumption really necessary? The expression þæt godcunde in cap. 1 above rather suggests that the author may have been familiar with foreign (ultimately Greek) constructions. For a short account of the influence of Greek on Old English see Stubbs, Mem. of St Dunstan, Intro. p. cxxii. Unfortunately there is nothing of St Dunstan’s composition extant which might be compared with these regulations, see Stubbs, op. cit. p. cix.
It has seemed necessary in translating to insert a phrase to complete the sense.
